title_en: Wang Liping v. Zhongmu County Transportation Bureau — dispute over administrative compensation
keywords_en: administrative; administrative compensation dispute; first instance; basic people's court; Henan Province; natural person; state organ; State Compensation Law; Highway Law; Henan Province Highway Management Regulations; legality of administrative vehicle seizure; causal relationship between damage and administrative act; elements of administrative compensation liability; partial support; vehicle seizure; death of live pigs; road maintenance fee collection; administrative compensation; Zhongmu County Transportation Bureau administrative compensation dispute
full_text_en:
Wang Liping v. Zhongmou County Communications Bureau — Dispute over Administrative Compensation

Plaintiff: Wang Liping, female, 44 years old, laid-off worker, residing in Xijiao Township, Kaifeng City, Henan Province.

Defendant: Zhongmou County Communications Bureau, Henan Province.

Legal Representative: Geng Xianming, Director of the Bureau.

The plaintiff, Wang Liping, filed an administrative compensation lawsuit with the Zhongmou County People's Court, Henan Province, due to a dispute over administrative compensation with the defendant, Zhongmou County Communications Bureau (hereinafter referred to as the County Communications Bureau).

The plaintiff alleged: On the morning of September 27, 2001, I borrowed three small four-wheel tractors from others and used two-wheel trailers to transport 31 live pigs. On the way, staff of the defendant demanded to impound the vehicles on the grounds that these three vehicles had not paid road maintenance fees. Although I explained that the goods loaded on the vehicles could not be left unattended and requested to unload the pigs before impounding, the defendant's staff ignored this, forcibly detached the trailers, and drove away, causing the pigs in the trailers to suffer from natural crushing and heatstroke due to the hot weather. A total of 15 pigs died, resulting in direct economic losses of RMB 10,500 and other losses of RMB 1,700. I applied to the defendant for compensation, but the defendant ignored it. I request the court to order the defendant to compensate me for all economic losses.

The plaintiff, Wang Liping, submitted the following evidence:

1. Testimony of Zhang Junming and Wang Laohu, mainly stating: On the morning of September 27, Wang Xianglin, Wang Xinchun, Zhang Junming, and Wang Laohu drove three small four-wheel tractors to help Wang Liping transport pigs. When the vehicles reached about one kilometer south of Xiwu Village, they encountered five staff members of the Local Highway Management Office of Zhongmou County Communications Bureau checking road maintenance fees. We explained that these were agricultural vehicles and had no maintenance fees. These people insisted on impounding the vehicles. At that time, Wang Liping said, "Please wait a moment, let us deliver the pigs to Dangzhuang Village, and we will handle the maintenance fee procedures upon return." These people still disagreed, forcibly started the vehicles and drove away, and we chased after them. When we caught up at the east intersection of Houheiguan Village, we negotiated with them again, asking them to drive two vehicles away and leave one for us, so that after we moved the pigs to Dangzhuang Village, they could drive away the remaining one. They disagreed and forcibly detached the three small four-wheel tractors from the trailers and drove away. It was around 11 a.m. at that time, the weather was very hot, there was no shade at the scene, and the pigs were crowded together in the trailers. Two pigs died on the spot.

2. Testimony of Ma Shujie, mainly stating: On September 27, Kaifeng Industrial Company came to my pig farm to collect pigs. Since the large truck for collecting pigs could not drive into Xiaodian Village, the pig collector notified Wang Liping to send the pigs to my pig farm. When Wang Liping was about two li away from my pig farm, the three small four-wheel tractors were driven away by people from the Local Highway Management Office of Zhongmou County Communications Bureau, and the trailers loaded with pigs were detached and left by the roadside. One end of the trailer was on the ground, and the vehicle body was severely tilted at a 45-degree angle. The pigs in the trailer were crowded together. Additionally, the temperature at that time was as high as over 30 degrees Celsius, there was no shade at the scene, and no water. The pigs suffered severely from heat, and two died on the spot. I called an agricultural vehicle to help Wang Liping first move the remaining pigs onto the agricultural vehicle, and then from the agricultural vehicle onto the two-tiered pig collection truck. At that time, more than ten pigs were barely alive. When the pig collection truck arrived at the Kaifeng pig transfer station and unloaded, 13 pigs had died. The remaining 16 pigs, due to severe fright and congestion throughout their bodies, were rejected by the Shanghai client and had to be sold at a low price in Kaifeng.

3. Testimony of Huo Xiaohuan, mainly stating: Around 10 a.m. that day, Ma Shujie asked me to help move pigs onto the pig collection truck. I drove there and only then learned that it was a woman from Xiaodian Village's pigs. The weather was quite hot at the time, and I saw that some pigs were already red from the heat, so I quickly unloaded the pigs from the small four-wheel trailer onto my vehicle and then reloaded them onto the large pig collection truck. While loading, I saw that one pig had already died and was thrown on the ground. Some pigs were nearly dead, and we loaded them onto the pig collection truck.

4. Certificate from the Kaifeng Suburban Animal Quarantine Station, mainly stating: At 3:40 p.m. on September 27, our station received a call from Zhang Baohong at the Kaifeng West Freight Yard Transfer Station reporting for inspection. We sent Lyu Hexing and Liu Xianzhong to conduct an on-site inspection and found that among the 29 pigs brought by Wang Liping from Zhongmou County, 13 had died. After inquiry and quarantine, it was determined that these 13 pigs died from heat. Our station then issued a quarantine certificate for the other pigs, allowing them to be transported.

5. Testimony of Zhang Baohong from Kaifeng Trade Industrial Company, mainly stating: On September 27, Wang Liping sold 16 live large pigs weighing 1,777 kg to our company at a price of RMB 6.60 per kg, totaling RMB 11,720.20, which was paid in full at the time.

6. An IOU written by Liu Yi, stating: Received 13 dead pigs from Wang Liping, each dead pig at RMB 30, total owed RMB 390.

7. A receipt, stating: On September 27, 2001, Wang Liping received RMB 11,720 for the sale of pigs.

8. Testimony of He Donggang, stating: From October 15 to December 27, 2001, Wang Liping rented my taxi to go to Zhongmou County on business, making more than 20 round trips, each trip costing RMB 80, totaling approximately RMB 1,700.

9. The *Zhengzhou Evening News* dated September 27, 2001, which reported that the highest daytime temperature in the Zhengzhou area that day was 24°C.

10. Wang Liping's compensation application and the receipt for the application issued by the Zhongmou County Communications Bureau.

The defendant argued: (1) In accordance with Article 36 of the *Highway Law of the People's Republic of China* and Article 53(2) of the *Regulations of Henan Province on Highway Administration*, our staff inspected and impounded three small four-wheel tractors driven by Wang Shutian, Wang Laohu, and Zhang Junmin, which had no road maintenance fee payment certificates. At the same time, we issued a *Notice of Traffic Violation* and a *Certificate of Temporary Impoundment of Vehicle* to the three individuals. Our staff acted lawfully, and the conduct was not improper. (2) The plaintiff hired the small four-wheel tractors to transport pigs, forming a contractual relationship with the tractor owners. The tractor owners had an obligation to safely transport the plaintiff's pigs to the destination. If the plaintiff suffered damage because the small four-wheelers were impounded for driving on the highway without paying maintenance fees, that damage was caused by the owners' illegal conduct. The plaintiff should claim compensation from the vehicle owners. There is no direct causal relationship between the damage the plaintiff alleges and the defendant's lawful administrative act. The defendant should not bear compensation liability, and the plaintiff's claim should be dismissed.

During the hearing, the defendant's attorney further argued: (3) The plaintiff used narrow small four-wheel trailers to transport pigs, with 10-11 pigs loaded in each trailer. Crushing would inevitably occur during transport, not solely due to the tilting of the trailers. When the vehicles were impounded, it was clear autumn weather with a temperature below 24°C, and the impoundment site was an open, ventilated field. Under such conditions, the plaintiff's claim that the pigs died from heatstroke lacks sufficient evidence. Furthermore, the impoundment site was less than 200 meters from the pig collection point where the plaintiff was heading. The plaintiff could have managed to deliver the pigs to the collection point but took no measures within three hours, watching the pigs die and allowing the losses to expand, which is incomprehensible. (4) The plaintiff sold the pigs to Kaifeng Trade Industrial Company in Dangzhuang Village, so ownership had already transferred. The death of pigs after arrival in Kaifeng has nothing to do with the plaintiff, and the plaintiff cannot claim compensation for this.

The defendant submitted the following evidence and legal bases:

1. Article 36(2) of the *Highway Law of the People's Republic of China* promulgated on July 3, 1997, which states: "Before the implementation of the fuel surcharge collection method, the current highway maintenance fee collection method shall continue to apply. Highway maintenance fees must be used for the maintenance and reconstruction of highways. Units and individuals who own vehicles and pay highway maintenance fees shall be issued a highway maintenance fee payment mark by the competent transportation department; the highway maintenance fee payment mark shall be placed in a conspicuous position on the vehicle. Vehicles without a highway maintenance fee payment mark shall not drive on the highway."

2. Article 53(2) of the *Regulations of Henan Province on Highway Administration* promulgated by the Standing Committee of the Eighth People's Congress of Henan Province on September 6, 1995, which states: "If a party fails to pay, evades, or refuses to pay highway maintenance fees in accordance with regulations, the competent transportation administrative department may temporarily impound the vehicle, and release the vehicle immediately after the party accepts the penalty."

3. Article 38 of the *Measures of Henan Province for the Administration of Highway Maintenance Fee Collection* issued by the Henan Provincial People's Government on June 6, 1994, which states: "For vehicles that are in arrears, overdue, refusing to pay, or resisting payment of maintenance fees, or have not been inspected, if on-site handling is not possible in a timely manner, the maintenance fee collection agency may temporarily impound the vehicle and its license plates, issue a *Certificate of Temporary Impoundment of Vehicle (Certificate) for Highway Maintenance Fee Violations* and an *On-site Traffic Administrative Penalty Decision*, and order the party to report to the designated maintenance fee collection agency for handling within 7 days from the date of impoundment."

4. *Notice of Traffic Violation* (Notice No. 16-18).

5. *Certificate of Temporary Impoundment of Vehicle* (Impoundment No. 16-18).

6. Records of inquiries with Wang Shutian, Zhang Junmin, Wang Laohu, and others.

7. *Report on Conclusion of Traffic Administrative Penalty* (Conclusion No. 16-18).

8. Testimony of Zhang Chunxiang, Zhang Xiuju, and Du Xiuhua, mainly stating: On the afternoon of September 27, Li Qingwei, an external inspector of the Second Inspection Team, sent three receipts for half-year road maintenance fees, each for RMB 720, asking us internal staff to issue invoices. The next afternoon, several people came and paid the RMB 720 maintenance fee per vehicle, raising no issues at the time. We then immediately processed the release procedures for the vehicles.

9. Testimony of Hu Guangyu, mainly stating: On September 27, the three small four-wheel tractors temporarily impounded by the Zhongmou County Agricultural Vehicle Maintenance Fee Collection Station were parked in the parking lot under my charge. The next day, these three vehicles were released.

Based on the evidence submitted by the plaintiff, the Zhongmou County People's Court investigated and inquired with witnesses Ma Shujie, Zhang Junming, Wang Laohu, Wang Xianglin, Wang Xinchun, Lyu Hexing, Liu Yi, Zhang Baohong, and others, each producing one investigation record. The content of each witness's account was consistent with the testimony they had provided to the plaintiff. Witness Liu Yi testified that he bought the 13 pigs that died from heat at RMB 30 each to feed his more than ten dogs.

After examination and authentication at trial, the Zhongmou County People's Court found that the above evidence was objective, truthful, and could corroborate each other, and was sufficient to serve as the basis for determining the facts of this case. Based on the evidence, the facts of this case were found as follows:

The plaintiff, Wang Liping, is a laid-off worker from the Kaifeng Metal Recycling Company and now operates a pig farm in Xiaodian Village, Dongzhang Township, Zhongmou County. On the morning of September 27, 2001, Wang Liping borrowed small four-wheel tractors from villagers Zhang Junming, Wang Laohu, and Wang Shutian in Xiaodian Village, loaded with 31 live pigs, and prepared to go to the pig collection point set up by Kaifeng Trade Industrial Company for sale. On the way, she encountered staff of the defendant, the County Communications Bureau, checking vehicles. After inspection, the staff of the County Communications Bureau, on the grounds that the vehicles had not paid road maintenance fees, served Zhang Junming, Wang Laohu, and Wang Shutian with a *Certificate of Temporary Impoundment of Vehicle*, then detached the three two-wheel trailers loaded with pigs, left them south of Heizhai Village, Cangzhai Township, and drove away the three small four-wheel tractors. After the detached two-wheel trailers lost the support of the tractor, they tilted at a 45-degree angle. The pigs inside the trailers could not stand and crowded to one side; two pigs died on the spot due to crushing and heat. With the help of Ma Shujie from Dangzhuang Village, Cangzhai Township, Wang Liping managed to transfer the remaining 29 pigs onto a pig collection truck. When the 29 pigs arrived in Kaifeng, another 13 had died. Wang Liping sold the 13 dead pigs to Liu Yi, an individual business operator in Kaifeng City, at RMB 30 per pig. On November 22 of the same year, Wang Liping applied to the County Communications Bureau for compensation but was refused. She then filed this lawsuit, requesting that the County Communications Bureau be ordered to compensate her for the loss of the dead pigs, RMB 10,500, and transportation costs, RMB 1,700.

The average weight of the live pigs sold by the plaintiff, Wang Liping, on this occasion was 110 kg per pig, with a value of RMB 6.6 per kg.

The Zhongmou County People's Court held:

The plaintiff, Wang Liping, claimed that the defendant's act of impounding the vehicles caused damage to her property. After applying to the County Communications Bureau for compensation without success, she filed an administrative compensation lawsuit. This conforms to the provisions of Article 67 of the *Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China* (hereinafter referred to as the Administrative Procedure Law) and should be accepted.

Administrative compensation is a type of state compensation. Only when the elements constituting administrative compensation liability are satisfied will the state bear compensation liability for damages caused by administrative torts. Therefore, in an administrative compensation lawsuit, determining the elements of administrative compensation liability is the primary issue.

The elements of administrative compensation liability include:

I. Subject of the tortious act: This refers to who performed the act that may give rise to administrative compensation liability. The *State Compensation Law of the People's Republic of China* (hereinafter referred to as the State Compensation Law) provides that the subjects that can become administrative tortfeasors mainly include: (1) administrative organs and their civil servants; (2) organizations authorized by laws or regulations and their staff; (3) organizations entrusted by administrative organs and their staff; (4) individuals entrusted by administrative organs.

The plaintiff, Wang Liping, alleged that the staff of the defendant, the County Communications Bureau, impounded the vehicles, causing her property losses. The County Communications Bureau is an administrative organ, and its staff are civil servants of the administrative organ. According to Article 3 of the State Compensation Law, the County Communications Bureau meets the element of being the subject of a tortious act.

II. Administrative illegal act: This refers to the nature of the act that may cause the state to bear administrative compensation liability. According to Articles 3, 4, and Article 5(1) of the State Compensation Law, the state is liable for compensation only when an administrative organ or its staff "infringes upon the lawful rights and interests of an administrative counterpart while exercising administrative powers"; the state does not bear compensation liability for "personal acts unrelated to the exercise of official powers" by administrative staff.

The legality of a specific administrative act includes not only clear findings of fact, correct application of law, and compliance with legal procedures, but also the reasonable exercise of administrative discretion by the administrative organ in the field of discretion. A specific administrative act that is manifestly unreasonable constitutes an abuse of discretion.

The small four-wheel tractors driven by Zhang Junming, Wang Laohu, and Wang Shutian were driving on the highway without paying road maintenance fees. Based on this fact, the staff of the defendant, the County Communications Bureau, made the decision to impound the vehicles. Since the administrative counterparts, Zhang Junming, Wang Laohu, Wang Shutian, or the plaintiff in this case, Wang Liping, did not dispute the decision to impound the vehicles, this case does not examine the legality of this decision.

The small four-wheel tractors scheduled for impoundment were in the process of transporting live pigs for the plaintiff, Wang Liping. Regardless of whether the decision to impound the vehicles was lawful, the staff of the defendant, the County Communications Bureau, when preparing to execute this decision, should have known that in hot weather, pigs in transit should not be crushed or left on the road for long. No matter who owned the pigs, only by properly handling them in a timely manner before impounding the vehicles could the property be prevented from suffering loss due to the impoundment. However, the staff of the County Communications Bureau did not consider the safety of the property, and even when Wang Liping requested that the pigs be delivered to the destination before impoundment, they ignored it, detached the two-wheel trailers, and drove away the tractors. This administrative act of the County Communications Bureau's staff in executing the decision to impound the vehicles does not meet the requirements of reasonableness and appropriateness and constitutes an abuse of discretion. Pursuant to Article 54(1)(ii)(5) of the Administrative Procedure Law and Article 57(2)(ii) of the *Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Implementation of the Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China*, the act of the County Communications Bureau's staff in exercising administrative powers should be confirmed as illegal.

III. Actual damage: This refers to the requirement that the illegal official act must have caused a certain consequence of damage before the state's administrative compensation liability is triggered. The "damage" mentioned here refers to damage to personal freedom, damage to life and health, and damage to property, and such damage should be actual damage that has occurred.

The plaintiff, Wang Liping's 15 live pigs died due to prolonged heat and crushing. This actual damage is sufficient to constitute a reason for claiming state compensation.

IV. Causation: This refers to the connection between the illegal official act and the consequence of damage that allows the state to bear administrative compensation liability.

The death of the plaintiff, Wang Liping's 15 live pigs due to prolonged heat and crushing was caused by the unreasonable and inappropriate administrative acts of the defendant, the County Communications Bureau's staff, when executing the decision to impound the vehicles. There is a causal relationship between the two. The administrative decision to impound the vehicles was executed by the staff of the County Communications Bureau on their own initiative, and the consequences arising from improper execution measures should naturally be borne by the County Communications Bureau.

In summary, the plaintiff, Wang Liping, suffered property damage due to the administrative act of the defendant, the County Communications Bureau's staff, constituting an abuse of discretion. Her lawsuit requesting compensation is lawful and should be upheld. After deducting RMB 390 from the sale of the dead pigs, Wang Liping's economic loss is RMB 10,500, and the County Communications Bureau should compensate her. Wang Liping also requested compensation for transportation costs of RMB 1,700, but the corresponding evidence she submitted to support this request could not be verified and authenticated; therefore, this part of the claim is not upheld. The evidence in this case is sufficient to prove that the 15 pigs died from being crushed and heated for a long time in the tilted trailers after the small four-wheel tractors were impounded; the impoundment site was far more than 200 meters from the pig collection point, and Wang Liping, without her vehicles being available for transport, could not ensure the safety of the pigs; selling pigs must undergo quarantine; how Wang Liping performed the quarantine procedures, how the transaction was concluded, and when ownership of the property transferred in her sale of pigs to Kaifeng Trade Industrial Company were matters within the scope of the parties' agreement and were not subject to interference by others; the pigs found dead after arrival in Kaifeng were also owned by Wang Liping. The County Communications Bureau's defenses—that Wang Liping should claim compensation from the small four-wheel tractor owners, that the evidence of the pigs dying from heatstroke was insufficient, that Wang Liping should not have sat by and allowed the losses to expand, and that she had no right to claim compensation for pigs that died after arrival in Kaifeng—are untenable. Accordingly, the Zhongmou County People's Court rendered the following judgment on March 19, 2002:

The act of the defendant, the County Communications Bureau, in impounding the three small four-wheel tractor heads borrowed by the plaintiff, Wang Liping, on the morning of September 27, 2001, which caused the death of Wang Liping's pigs, is illegal.

The defendant, the County Communications Bureau, shall compensate the plaintiff, Wang Liping, for economic losses in the amount of RMB 10,500 within three days from the date this judgment takes effect.

Litigation costs of RMB 430 shall be borne by the defendant, the County Communications Bureau.

After the judgment was pronounced, neither party appealed, and the judgment of first instance became legally effective.
